REPUBLIC OF KENYA
IN THE HIGH COURT OF KENYA AT NAKURU
FAMILY DIVISION
SUCCESSION CAUSE NO. E331 OF 2025
BETWEEN
IN THE MATTER OF THE ESTATE OF JKM (DECEASED) ........ 
AND
MWK ........ APPLICANT
AND
PNM ........ RESPONDENT
RULING
Coram: Hon. Justice S. K. Barasa-Lemiso
Delivered on 20th August 2026
1. This ruling concerns an application by MWK, the widow of the deceased, for an order directing that survivors' benefits payable by the National Social Security Fund be held in trust for the three minor children of the deceased. The names of the parties and children are anonymised to protect the children.
2. The deceased, a member of the Fund, died on 11th January 2025. The Respondent, PNM, who describes herself as a second wife under customary law, objects and asks that the benefit be shared equally between the two households.
3. The Fund has filed a statement confirming that a survivors' pension and a funeral grant are payable, under sections 37 and 40 respectively of the National Social Security Fund Act, 2013, and that it will abide by the directions of the court.
4. Medical records produced by the Applicant show that the youngest child has a chronic medical condition requiring monthly treatment. The court has considered these records only for the purpose of assessing need and directs that they be sealed.
5. Article 53(2) of the Constitution requires that a child's best interests are of paramount importance in every matter concerning the child. The court must also have regard to the Children Act, 2022.
6. The question whether the Respondent is a dependant within the meaning of the Law of Succession Act is a matter for the hearing of the cause and cannot be resolved on affidavit evidence.
7. Pending that hearing, the survivors' pension shall be paid into an interest-earning account in the joint names of the advocates for both parties, and KES 45,000 per month shall be released to the Applicant for the maintenance of the minors.
8. The funeral grant, having already been applied to the funeral expenses, is not in issue.
9. Costs shall be in the cause.
S. K. BARASA-LEMISO
JUDGE
